## You Don’t Mess with the Zohan: One of the Best Sessions of Restorative Escapism

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ne-shutite-s-zokhanom-2008/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-27 (27 June 2026)
Work: “You Don’t Mess with the Zohan” is a 2008 film directed by Dennis Dugan.
Tags: comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ne-shutite-s-zokhanom-2008/

I’d never have thought that one of my best sessions of restorative escapism would turn out to be watching ***You Don’t Mess with the Zohan***.

The plot, about a counter-terrorist (Adam Sandler) who has grown tired of fighting and faked his own death to start a new life, may seem single-layered. Perhaps its strength lies precisely in laying all its between-the-lines meanings out in plain view, leaving each viewer to pick the main ones as far as they care to. And yes, I was bought with hummus jokes. Yes, I watched it in the original, so I fell for the accents as well ([sue me](https://t.me/kino_voice/1213)). Yes, the film’s humour runs dark and belongs more in the “on the edge of good taste” category (if you’ve seen *Borat*, it’s comparable). All of that is redeemed by one gigantic “but”, which those who have seen it can probably name with ease, and those who haven’t (I envy you now) will surely be able to spot as they watch.

For all its frivolity, this is a film that doubles as a social utopia, about what we so long for in the world and find so impossible to achieve. Everyone does what they love. Disagreements are a thing of the past. The most barbed remarks aimed at your neighbour are flagged in advance as jokes (and invite ribbing in return). I don’t know how this film passed me by back in the day, but it found me at perhaps the best possible moment — and I hope it will brighten one of your evenings.

---

## Baranyi bega: Guy Ritchie Charm and an Off-the-Charts Number of Jokes

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/barani-bega-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026)
Work: “Baranyi bega” is a 2026 series directed by Rashid Yusupov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/barani-bega-serial/

***Baranyi bega*** («Бараньи бега», “The Ram Races”) packs some off-the-charts number of genuinely funny jokes into every square centimetre: scripted ones, visual ones and even ones made in the edit.

This is a story with pure Guy Ritchie charm. Two meat deliverymen in Dagestan are driving a load of (by the looks of it, stolen) mutton to a hotel opening, but they get a little carried away watching wrestling, so the trip drags on. A bag of money drops on them from a plane carrying some Russian gangsters from Georgia. Not that the butcher brothers even get the chance to find out about it. At the very first stop the bag (along with the mutton) is stolen from the back of the truck by the hapless prop mistress of a local film crew (and film people, as the deliverymen put it, are more dangerous than Gypsies).

In short, it all gets tangled up at a very brisk pace, and from one joke to the next the audience practically never stopped laughing. I’ll be waiting for it on streaming.

---

## Problem Child: Palpable Madness and an Absolute Must-Watch Series

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026); updated: 2026-10-08
Work: “Problem Child” is a 2026 series directed by Vladimir Bolgov, Velimir Rusakov, Nikita Zubkov.
Tags: series, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/

## 20 June 2026

***Problem Child*** (*Trudny rebyonok*) is either experimental absurdism or an absurd experiment. But it makes for a magnificent watch.

Professional footballer Filipp (Gennady Blinov) accidentally breaks his leg and finds himself having to raise money for an operation, so he picks up work on the side, now in petty crime, now as a history tutor. And along the way everything turns out so insanely that the comedy moves up to the level of some kind of full-blown meta-humour, which is very enticing. And with Mujuice on the soundtrack, too. I really want to see what comes next: I was howling with laughter.

## 25 September 2026

I’m watching [*Problem Child*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1764) with a kind of half-forgotten gusto

The series has such a distinct, palpable air of madness and derangement that it plunges you into an unnatural kind of viewing comfort. Perhaps it would even be fair to call it “ecstasy”: wow, someone on screen has things even more unhinged than in real life. But even in such a strange, upside-down world there is room for love (all ages and all walks of life really do yield to it), friendship and optimism. And suddenly the story of an injured footballer who tutors on the side so that he can have an operation and get back into the sport takes on new colours.

And every one of the actors is exactly where they belong: from now on I’ll definitely be following the work of Gennady Blinov (the footballer-historian) and Boris Deikov (the problem child himself).

A wonderful piece of work, and one with a personality of its own next to many comedy series.

## 8 October 2026

I’ve finished [*Problem Child*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1788), and now I can say with confidence that it is an absolute must-watch of a series.

Beyond what has already been praised in the posts above, there is something else worth noting. This is a rare case of a series whose pace neither sags nor breaks down in the middle of the season (a rarity these days): you never feel the urge to drop it or skip ahead to the end. Form here is in complete harmony with content: absurdity in both, but very well balanced. A special bow to the writers for the genuine urge to keep a notebook of quotes while watching.

And the footballer-historian joins my personal collection of characters of the “you don’t want to be with him, you want to be him” kind. Stay tuned for updates.

---

## Vor v zagone: A Sweet Comedy, and Kudos for Popularising Psychology

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vor-v-zagone-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-20 (20 June 2026)
Work: “Vor v zagone” is a 2026 series directed by Artyom Lempert.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vor-v-zagone-serial/

***Vor v zagone*** («Вор в загоне», “Thief in the Pen”, a pun on *vor v zakone*, “thief in law”) is the very project from Russian Code with Denis Vlasenko that I [had pinned my hopes on](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/).

Anton, a psychologist (Denis Vlasenko), travels with his girlfriend Polina to Ust-Baikalsk to meet her parents. Nothing goes to plan, and the head of the family (Vladimir Vdovichenkov) takes offence at Anton. The young man goes out to the garage to try to build a rapport with him and discovers that he is holding someone hostage. The head of the family decides to test him and takes him along to torture the hostage, but through Anton’s fault the hostage gets away. In the process Vdovichenkov’s character has a panic attack, and Anton helps him come round, but he still won’t accept the young man. It turns out that Polina is pregnant, so Anton and the father of the family have to put their differences aside.

It’s a sweet comedy, every actor is in the right place, and above all, kudos for popularising psychology and care for mental health. I’ll be waiting for it.

---

## Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek: A Realistic Conversation with the Audience on Equal Terms

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/alyosha-bozhiy-chelovek-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek” is a 2026 series directed by Mikhail Chistov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/alyosha-bozhiy-chelovek-serial/

Okko (the Russian streaming service) has struck up an interesting conversation about important subjects on screen with the series ***Alyosha Bozhiy chelovek*** («Алёша Божий человек», “Alyosha, Man of God”; out of competition).

Its makers call the show a “cousin” of [*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/). The pilot centres on an ordinary grandmother who was nearly killed by her own young grandson. She begins to wonder in all seriousness whether the boy has been possessed by demons and tries to persuade her daughter that he must be taken to a monastery, but in the end takes matters into her own hands.

This is no tedious moralising tract and no comedy, but a very realistic conversation with the audience on equal terms. The camera peeks into the kitchens of the grandmothers who have their kulich (Easter cake) blessed every Easter, and of the young parents who, because of their circumstances, have grown somewhat indifferent to bringing up their children. As Gavriil Gordeev says, the series lets us witness the everyday judgement directed at all of them, which we feel ourselves but don’t notice in daily life. We all know these people, and that kind of accuracy on screen is striking — I hope we’ll get to see more soon.

---

## Klyatva Gippokrata: The Ambulance Service as a String of Funny Incidents

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/klyatva-gippokrata-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Klyatva Gippokrata” is a 2026 series directed by Nikita Andrienko.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/klyatva-gippokrata-serial/

And here is the close-knit team, all in merch, that presented the series ***Klyatva Gippokrata*** («Клятва Гиппократа», “The Hippocratic Oath”)

Viktor Zhivykh (Konstantin Beloshapka), a cocky young surgeon, is packed off by the chief physician (Pavel Derevyanko) to work on an ambulance as a punishment. His new colleagues, the paramedic Lyonya (Egor Ovchinnikov) and the driver Nikolaich (Andrey Fedortsov), give the newcomer a friendly induction into this new world (and help to reform the insolent Zhivykh while they’re at it).

Ambulance work in this series is more a string of funny incidents than the tough job of saving lives. But those are the conventions of the genre, and on its own terms the show is very enjoyable — I’ll be watching it to the end.

---

## Sokrovishcha skifov: A Solid Adventure Drama with Meme-Worthy Moments

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/sokrovischa-skifov-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-19 (19 June 2026)
Work: “Sokrovishcha skifov” is a 2026 series directed by Evgeniy Bedarev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, adventure
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/sokrovischa-skifov-serial/

***Sokrovishcha skifov*** («Сокровища скифов», “Treasures of the Scythians”) is a solid adventure drama inspired, according to its creators, by *Indiana Jones*.

As a television series it is a fairly interesting piece of work. Linda Lapiņš plays Katya, a principled archaeologist, and around her and her son, who has developed an interest in archaeology, a fight for an ancient gold artefact unfolds. But the most unusual thing is a handful of utterly meme-worthy moments that don’t look as if they were deliberately tied into the story. A bodyguard with John Travolta’s face, gold stashed among the pelmeni (Russian dumplings) in the freezer, a packet of crisps that migrates to the bin and back. In short, I think I’ll be watching the next episodes :)

---

## Affekt: A Minimalist Thriller That Deserves a Chance from Genre Fans

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/affekt-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Affekt” is a 2026 series directed by Vladislav Andreev.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, thriller
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/affekt-serial/

On the evidence of its first episode, the series *Affekt* («Аффект», “Affect”) plays like a minimalist, high-concept psychological thriller.

Kirill, an ordinary taxi driver, unwittingly causes the death of a scooter rider. He falls into a state of affect (a fit of passion, in the legal sense) and — whether in his head or for real — meets a talkative investigator, who tells him the story of an accidental killing exactly like his own, complete with a way to cover it up. The moment he has parted with his passenger, the driver rushes to put what he has heard into practice, and that is how he gets mixed up with the criminal world.

One undeniable strength is its sustained visual resemblance to the film *Centaur* («Кентавр»). Beyond that there are pluses and minuses, but it definitely deserves a chance from fans of the genre.

---

## Jive: An Heir to On the Ice and the Brutal Side of Sport as Spectacle

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dzhayv-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Jive” is a 2026 series directed by Danil Chashchin.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, sport, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/dzhayv-serial/

***Jive*** is in many ways an heir to *On the Ice*, another high-energy series from Okko (the Russian streaming service) about the brutal side of sport as spectacle.

In Moscow, a fierce rivalry is playing out between the strongest ballroom couples. Each dancer has their own backstory, their own dream and (let’s be honest) their own nervous breakdown, but not all of them know that their own coach may be taking money to tilt the judging towards someone else’s dancers. Meanwhile, David Sokratyan’s character runs away from a remote village — literally on an ancient motorcycle with a sidecar. He is the one who sets off a chain of changes in the dancers’ close-knit ~~community~~ snake pit.

I’ll keep watching; I’m curious to see where it goes.

---

## Second Wind: A Story That Gets Under Your Skin

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “Second Wind” is a 2026 series directed by Ruslan Bratov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/

The pilot episode of ***Second Wind*** from Okko (the Russian streaming service) makes an incredible impression ([as I suspected it would](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/)).

They are trying to pack Ilya (Alexander Pal) off to a motivational centre to cure him of his addiction. From the moment he is through the door, it turns out to be an absurd, cruel world with rules that lie beyond human empathy. A name alone is not enough to introduce yourself, because it must always be followed by the label “alcoholic” or “drug addict” — depending on the dependency. Ilya refuses to admit to any such thing, sets himself against the whole way of life there and starts plotting his escape.

The show is very strong, and not only in its ideas and its chosen subject. The visual touches (the many nods to *Fight Club*, for example) and the 4:3 frame — “cramped”, just like the hero’s confined circumstances — persuade you on a subconscious level. In the same way, the whole story seems to work its way under your skin, leaving you no chance of tearing yourself away. Seeing it through is a must.

---

## Living Anew: A Time-Travel Comedy That Slipped Out Suspiciously Quietly

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/zhizn-zanovo-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026); updated: 2026-11-04
Work: “Living Anew” is a 2026 series directed by Aleksandr Boguslavskiy.
Tags: series, streaming
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/zhizn-zanovo-serial/

## 18 June 2026

**Living Anew** (*Zhizn zanovo*), one of the shows I had been [looking forward to](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/) with interest, has fully lived up to expectations.

This time-travel comedy comes across as a thoroughly entertaining, solid piece of work. Alexander Yatsenko is very convincing as an ambulance doctor worn down by life and by his own failings, as *Arrhythmia* showed, and the series makes 100% use of that advantage. The humour is charming and fresh, so it is a great pleasure to watch.

A broken MRI machine sends the present-day hero back to 2002, and the panorama of 2000s St Petersburg, set to Glukoza (the Russian pop singer), simply takes your breath away. *The Stroll* is playing at the cinema, and every student has a pager on their belt. The hero himself lands in that time with everything he has learned in his 40 years, and puts it to use in his own way.

A super project that I will be waiting for impatiently and will definitely watch to the end.

## 4 November 2026

[*Living Anew*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1558) has landed on streaming suspiciously quietly, and I am still watching it, just as I had planned to ever since Pilot (the Russian series festival).

It is all nicely done, well paced (perfect for watching several episodes in a row!) and free of the dreary clichés that come with the time-travel genre. Its moral compass wobbles a bit, but in 2002 Dima the doctor (Alexander Yatsenko/Anton Shavrin) tirelessly wriggles out of one scrape after another while trying not to set off the notorious butterfly effect, and he does it rather wittily. Compliments to the script and the costume designers: the wardrobe of Lenya, the hero’s best friend, is so stylish that you want to swipe the whole lot for personal use in 2026.

The main strength, which emerges after a few episodes, is the perfect casting of the characters’ younger and older selves. Anton Shavrin (the young version of Yatsenko) wonderfully conveys the state of a forty-year-old doctor trapped in the body of an 18-year-old student — a real find. Robert Zakharyan, who plays Artyom Tkachenko’s character in 2002, is a terrific comic type altogether; I hope he gets to show more of that. And I really like the heroines in their youth: Alisa and Kristina are played by Elizaveta Ishchenko and Margarita Dyachenkova (I have followed her for a long time, as we have known each other since school), and each has an elusive intonation borrowed from her adult counterpart (Karina Razumovskaya and Elena Podkaminskaya respectively).

I have a few final episodes left for dessert, and I am making them last as long as I can.

---

## ZhPT: AI Can Do a Lot, but Creative Execution Is a Human Privilege

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/zhpt-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-18 (18 June 2026)
Work: “ZhPT” is a 2026 series directed by Yana Rubanovskaya.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, documentary
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/zhpt-serial/

The intriguing show ***ZhPT*** («ЖПТ», a play on “GPT” in Russian letters) is devoted to unconventional ways of using neural networks.

The host, Karen Adamyan, travels around Russian cities and explores how local businesses, manufacturers and ordinary people can be helped by building artificial intelligence into what they do. It is shot in the best traditions of the travel show, and it also raises digital literacy, popularises neural networks and adds to their good name. In the first episode a luge coach, a restaurant owner and an architect from Kandalaksha were introduced to AI. And Karen himself dived into icy water, having secured the support of a neural-network psychologist in his earpiece.

I hope the show finds its target audience — the mix of themes is an unusual one. The main thing is that its guiding idea is a very well-balanced one: a neural network can think up or optimise a great deal, but giving an idea creative form and making it real is always a human right and privilege.

---

## Pilot 2026: Independent Projects I Want to See in Full

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-17 (17 June 2026); updated: 2026-06-22
Tags: festivals, series, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/

## 17 June 2026

I’m plunging into the film-festival atmosphere: [Pilot](https://t.me/kino_voice/1514) (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) is starting, which means that over the next 5 days this channel will fill up with reviews of the first episodes of all kinds of series.

I went through the (very hefty) programme in advance and noted down the shows whose descriptions sound most interesting.

- ***Vor v zagone*** («Вор в загоне», “A Thief in the Pen”, a play on *vor v zakone*, “thief in law”): a series with Denis Vlasenko (you remember my [principles](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pro-eto-samoe-serial/)). A comedy about a psychologist who studies his fiancée’s relatives and assigns each of them a mental disorder of their own. I’m hoping for *About This Very Thing* with a psychological slant

- ***Festival*** («Фестиваль»): a series about a film festival, and what could be better than watching something like that at a film festival?! The director is Alexey Kamynin, who previously made the wonderful and very funny film *Russian Spleen* («Хандра»). The cast of the new show includes Daniil Vorobyov, Mikhail Troynik and, incidentally, my colleague [Artyom Remizov](https://t.me/remizorro)

- ***Second Wind***: a tragicomedy by Ruslan Bratov with Alexander Pal, about trying to find yourself in life and difficult relationships with the people closest to you. I trust Bratov to tell this story in a dramatically funny way.

- ***Jive***: a high-energy show about dancesport from the production company Sreda for Okko (the Russian streaming service), so I expect the quality to match. The cast includes David Sokratyan, Anastasia Ukolova, Svyatoslav Rogozhan and lots of cool young actors.

- ***Living Anew***: a comedy about a second chance to live your best years (literally and figuratively: the main character is transported from the present day to 2002). The cast includes Alexander Yatsenko, Elena Podkaminskaya and other actors you always believe. Shades of [*Comeback*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kambek-serial/), judging by the era.

- ***Pasha*** with Askar Ilyasov ([I wrote about it here](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))

## 18 June 2026

The block of independent projects has been shown, and here are the ones I hope we will get to see in full in the future:

**GBU “Zhizn”** («ГБУ „Жизнь“», “State Institution ‘Life’”)

As the team behind the project put it, “we talk about traditional values in a non-traditional way”. The series will be about an unusual funeral home that tries to make even the part of life that has to do with death life-affirming. A gentle, blackish (naturally) but very likeable comedy.

***Volshebnaya pyl*** («Волшебная пыль», “Magic Dust”)

A talented chemist (Yulia Volkova) loses her job and suddenly discovers that her neighbour is cooking up something suspicious. Having ruined the neighbour’s homemade-cosmetics business with her vigilance, the woman is plotting something.

***Vverkh za mechtoy*** («Вверх за мечтой», “Up After the Dream”)

A romantic comedy with Polina Denisova and Grisha Vernik. An underrated producer finds herself forced to work with an arrogant showman (a former university classmate, to boot), but their hostility gradually gives way to passion. The “enemies to lovers” mechanism works brilliantly on screen, and I have known one of the producers, Liza Bulatova, since school, so I believe in this story.

***Privet, Karolinka*** («Привет, Каролинка», “Hi, Karolinka”)

A children’s adventure fantasy about a girl who investigates her grandmother’s mysterious disappearance with the help of a magic piece of chalk. What sets the project apart is that the main villain is played by the stylist Alexander Rogov. A spiritual heir to *Curious Varvara* (the children’s detective series), which makes it a bid for a quality children’s series.

## 19 June 2026

The morning starts with independent projects: today it’s sci-fi, aliens and mockumentary.

*Shisha*

A project about provincial evil spirits who live in the age of social media and decide to relaunch their villainous brand to keep the “Agency of Dirty Tricks” from being shut down. For this, “Kolkhoz Production” is brought in. A little raw (which is perfectly normal for the pilot of an independent project), but already a very charming spiritual heir to *What We Do in the Shadows* and *The Magic District* (*Volshebny uchastok*).

*Kosmos nash* (“Space Is Ours”)

A blogger who films so-called contactees (people who have made contact with aliens) hits a million subscribers and suddenly loses his dog. What he gains instead is a suspicious fangirl with the habits of an alien. Another pilot that is likeable at the concept level and has every chance of success once it has been polished.

## 19 June 2026

Two decent TV shows: ***Angel*** («Ангел») from TV-3 and ***Ilya Murovets*** («Илья Муровец», a play on the epic hero Ilya Muromets and MUR, the Moscow criminal investigation department) from Channel 5 (both are Russian TV channels).

In *Angel*, Kuzma Saprykin plays the angel Serafim, sent down from heaven to watch over an investigator who has recently lost her husband. A nod of sorts to the film *Moy paren angel* («Мой парень ангел», “My Boyfriend Is an Angel”). It sticks in the memory for the perfect choice of actor for the angel, and also for comic moments teetering between cringe and wisdom (I noted down, for instance, the line “if someone has wiped their feet on you once, don’t go rolling yourself back up like a worn-out doormat” — the audience applauded).

*Ilya Murovets* is a police procedural with a fairy-tale accent. It’s all just as the Channel 5 people described it at the morning industry session: a fairy tale according to Propp, magical helpers and a happy ending. The only thing that lets it down is the none-too-polished AI-generated inserts of the hero’s flashbacks to his past.

## 20 June 2026

Today’s block of independent projects delighted me with its youth themes:

***Kod 102*** («Код 102», “Code 102”)

Possibly the strongest independent project of the year. A vibey, neon-lit series about young musicians from Ufa who are trying to break through and make their dream come true. The project has its distinctive features: the local colour of Bashkortostan and Ufa, the involvement of local performers, and an excellent cast: Chingiz Garaev, Arseny Kasperovich, Pyotr Skvortsov and other cool actors.

***#Ne\_moya\_zhizn*** («#Не\_моя\_жизнь», “#Not_My_Life”)

A story about the destructive effect of social media on our lives, told through teenage characters. A high-school girl who dreams of becoming a blogger happens to find a phone and starts posting videos from it. After that everything starts going her way, but as soon as the owner demands the phone back, things stop being pleasant.

***Tozhe mne lyubov*** («Тоже мне любовь», “Call That Love”)

A drama about different kinds of relationships: between romantic partners, between sisters, with yourself. All of them, naturally, unhealthy. It plays very much in the spirit of the recent [*Half Man*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/half-man-serial/).

## 21 June 2026

And two more projects that struck me as promising:

***The Captain’s Daughter*** («Капитанская дочка»): a fresh screen adaptation of the classic with Oleg Savostyuk, Evgeny Tkachuk, Viktoria Isakova and other heavyweight actors. It sounds interesting and looks striking; what remains to be seen is how it will be pitched.

***Kamenskaya. Reboot*** («Каменская. Перезагрузка»): a relaunch of the classic series (the 2000s detective show based on Alexandra Marinina’s novels) with Yulia Khlynina in the lead. She was excellent as the investigator in [*Overheard in Rybinsk*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/podslushano-v-rybinske-serial/), so I believe in this character too.

## 21 June 2026

All the winners of Pilot 2026

- Best series pilot: [*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/)
- Best series pilot (audience choice): [*Problem Child*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/trudnyy-rebenok-serial/)
- Best director of a series pilot: Ruslan Bratov ([*Second Wind*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vtoroe-dykhanie-serial/))
- Best pilot screenplay: Anton Kolomeets and Evgeniya Tamakhina ([*Pasha*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))
- Best ensemble cast: the series [*Festival*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1597) («Фестиваль»)
- Best actor in a series: Askar Ilyasov ([*Pasha*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/))
- Best actress in a series: Yulianna Mikhnevich (she appeared in three of the festival’s series)
- Best documentary series: [*Virus popsy*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1556) («Вирус попсы», “The Pop Virus”)
- Best second season of a series: [*Old School*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1574)
- Most anticipated series: *Krasnaya shambala* («Красная шамбала», “Red Shambhala”)

## 22 June 2026

Pilot 2026 has wrapped up, and [Olya](https://t.me/hightechlowlifee) and I have put together all the festival’s series for Kinopoisk (Russia’s largest film database, media and streaming service) [in a single roundup](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4012907/).

This year’s programme is (to my taste) a strong one, and I have been sharing my most vivid impressions here throughout the festival. And in the piece, do pay attention to the award-winning series: they are an absolute must-watch on every count (Askar Ilyasov personally advised me to watch *Pasha*, which starts on 10 July, all the way to the end, so there is every reason to trust the tip).

## 22 June 2026

And I can’t help sharing this: I’ve come back from Pilot charged up for a whole year ahead with love of cinema, joy, and the energy to share my favourite series and support their premieres.

The strongest of programmes, the most caring organisation and a practically family atmosphere: every year I’m amazed at how good it is, and about an hour after the closing I start looking forward to next year. That, it seems to me, is unique and priceless.

I value beyond measure the chance to be part of something this lively, the trust of the organisers and your patience, dear readers (let’s be honest, a flood of posts like this doesn’t happen often). Thank you.

---

## Eto bylo v Rossii: A Patchwork Quilt of Musical and Media Culture

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/eto-bylo-v-rossii-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-15 (15 June 2026)
Work: “Eto bylo v Rossii: muzyka 2010-kh ot kalyan-repa do postpanka” is a 2025 book by Arkady Romanov.
Tags: books, music
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/eto-bylo-v-rossii-kniga/

And here’s another bookish one: I’ve made it through practically all (sorry, skipped chapter on chanson) of the non-fiction book [*Eto bylo v Rossii*](https://books.yandex.ru/books/yRjtQWuE) («Это было в России», “It Happened in Russia”).

An extremely absorbing text, packed with facts and yet weightless. Many of the songs it mentions are familiar to us from Russian series (the book devotes almost a whole chapter to the electronic musician Mujuice, a regular of *Peace! Friendship! Chewing Gum!*, the 1990s-set series).

Arkady Romanov ties Russia’s recent history to the biographies of the leading artists on the Russian scene and to social phenomena that we all lived through but haven’t reflected on enough. That is how a patchwork quilt of musical and media culture gets stitched together — a culture that, even from a short distance, is extremely interesting to relive.

---

## Pasha: A Handcrafted Island of Calm in a World of Adrenaline-Fuelled Content

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pasha-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-15 (15 June 2026); updated: 2026-08-04
Work: “Pasha” is a 2026 series directed by Anton Kolomeets, Evgeniya Tamakhina.
Tags: series, dramedy, Russian cinema
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/pasha-serial/

## 15 June 2026

A charming trailer for [*Pasha*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MU5Z6wX_oVQ), the upcoming series from Amediateka (a Russian streaming service)

The dramedy, starring Askar Ilyasov, will tell the story of Pasha Belov, a modest piano tuner: he was born in Moscow and studied at the Gnesinka (Moscow’s renowned Gnessin music school), but never did become a musician, and he can’t find out anything about his Uzbek roots. I’m glad the series takes on a subject that Russian films and series don’t often talk about: what it is like to be “one of us” and yet constantly run up against being read as an outsider. Genre-wise, by the looks of it, it will be a coming-of-age story, a conversation about identity and a sketch of a Muscovite’s life all at once. Irina Gorbacheva and Tatyana Dogileva also star, so the cast should be a treat.

I’ll write up the first episode from the [Pilot](https://t.me/kino_voice/1514) festival (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo) very soon, and the series premieres on 10 July.

## 20 June 2026

Once again, a team in merch (now I want some!!): Amediateka (a Russian streaming service) presents the series **Pasha** from my [list](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pilot-2026-nezavisimye-proekty/) of things to look forward to.

Judging by the first episode, this is a very touching, sparkling dramedy, gentle in its humour and its tone. Pasha, a Muscovite who is half Uzbek (and so comes up against every stereotype going), is trying to find somewhere to stay for 10 days, because a friend of his mother’s has moved into his own flat with a child who has chickenpox (and Pasha, as luck would have it, has never had it). So the hero literally and figuratively cannot find a home in his own home town.

As the show’s makers said, Askar Ilyasov is in every scene of the series. And I’ll add that he sets the tone and mood for everything that happens, and that creates something quite inimitable. It premieres on 10 July, and I can’t wait.

## 14 July 2026

I’ve carried on with [*Pasha*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1590) after seeing the first episode at Pilot (the Russian series festival in Ivanovo), and got exactly what I expected.

The series has a tone that is rare these days, that of those lyrical comedies where nothing especially funny seems to happen — sometimes quite the opposite, something sad — and yet every now and then you find yourself smiling. Simply because life takes its course, the sun peeks through the clouds, the neighbours act up and the relatives are being toxic. Life doesn’t end there, after all.

I’ll be watching closely for another reason too: Askar Ilyasov has promised something special in episode seven. Given that every episode of *Pasha* feels like a handcrafted island of calm in a world of adrenaline-fuelled content, I’m inclined to trust that tip.

## 4 August 2026

I finished all the episodes of [*Pasha*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1641) in one go and had the loveliest evening.

Askar Ilyasov promised that something special awaited us in episode 7, and he wasn’t lying: it is the peak of the season for how convincing and sincere it is, and for the absence of any sense of a boundary between the two sides of the screen. But personally I was most moved by episode 6 — whether it was the images of a Moscow school in the 2000s that struck a nerve, or the rare chance that materialises before little Pasha to replay an unhappy scenario, this time with a happy outcome (in the best traditions of modern psychology).

Either way, I highly recommend watching *Pasha*: its value lies not only in the character of the protagonist but also in the scattering of types around him. Every supporting character is genuinely distinctive and interesting; all of them, to borrow a line from children’s fiction, are “alive and glowing”. A rare feeling for a contemporary series.

---

## Filming Begins on the Series Moshennik. Istoriya klouna with Lev Zulkarnaev

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/moshennik-istoriya-klouna-semki/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-10 (10 June 2026)
Work: “Moshennik. Istoriya klouna” is a work  Anton Fedorov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, announcements
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/moshennik-istoriya-klouna-semki/

I see a show with Lev Zulkarnaev, I put it on my watchlist

Shooting has begun on ***Moshennik. Istoriya klouna*** («Мошенник. История клоуна», “The Swindler: A Clown’s Story”) from START and Premier (Russian streaming services). It’s an adventure drama about a provincial circus performer who is out for revenge after someone dear to him is swindled, joins a gang of phone scammers and then becomes a brilliant con artist himself. If you can’t beat them, lead them, as the saying goes.

I’ve been waiting a long time for new leading roles for Lev Zulkarnaev; I’ve missed them ever since [*She’s So Cool*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ona-takaya-klassnaya-serial/) (*Ona takaya klassnaya*). The director is Anton Fedorov, the man responsible for *Peace! Friendship! Chewing Gum!*, so expectations are high on every front. The cast will also include Kseniya Treyster, Efim Belosorochka, Evgeniya Simonova, Konstantin Murzenko, Vlad Tsenyov and many others. I’m waiting with all my might.

---

## My ne znakomimsya: Everyone Has a Lot in Common with the Alt Kids

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/my-ne-znakomimsya-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-10 (10 June 2026)
Work: “My ne znakomimsya” is a 2026 film directed by Yulia Guskova.
Tags: Russian cinema, documentary, Moscow, festival films
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/my-ne-znakomimsya-2026/

They’ve made a film about the alt kids (*nefory*, Russian slang for teenagers from alternative subcultures).

More precisely, the documentary [*My ne znakomimsya*](https://beatfilmfestival.ru/movies/my-ne-znakomimsya) («Мы не знакомимся», “We Don’t Make Acquaintances”) from the programme of Beat Film 2026 (the Moscow documentary film festival). For almost an hour we watch an ordinary day in the life of the young people who hang out at Kitay-Gorod (a central Moscow neighbourhood and metro hub). For anyone who spent time there when they were young, it’s a portal into the past; for those who don’t know the place, simply an atmospheric trip into a little world of its own.

The film has practically no plot; what spreads across the screen instead is a very tangible feeling of having absolutely no idea what comes next, on the scale of a whole life. As soon as it strikes you that the young are not the only ones tormented by doubts like these, you realise at once that everyone has a lot in common with the alt kids, and that being alt isn’t the point at all.

Of the standout moments, as someone with a hopeless sense of direction I especially appreciated the attempt to explain to a comrade who had gone astray how to get from exit 8 to where he needed to be. I hope he made it (I wouldn’t have).

## Luca: Incredible Beauty, Both in How It Looks and in What It Means

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/luka-2021/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-09 (9 June 2026)
Work: “Luca” is a 2021 film directed by Enrico Casarosa.
Tags: animation, rewatch
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/luka-2021/

*Silenzio Bruno!*

The part of my brain in charge of the holidays arriving on schedule told me to rewatch Pixar’s **Luca**. I have things to share:

- This is a very underrated film. Incredible beauty, both in how it looks and in what it means. It was worth rewatching if only for one thought: people who can accept us even as sea monsters (read: as ourselves) do exist!

- After my first viewing I actually had no memory of Luca himself being a sea monster too. I was sure he had merely made friends with one :) The Mandela effect has never been so personal.

- Respect for the way the film shows boys growing up: through friendship, vulnerability, curiosity and the right to be weird. Luca and Alberto grow up not because they get tougher but because they learn to listen to themselves and each other. For a healthy coming-of-age story, that is just the thing.

- This is one of the few Pixar works that don’t push their “grown-up side” to the fore the way, say, both [*Inside Out*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/golovolomka-2-2024/) films or *Soul* do (with all due respect). Here, on the contrary, they play a game with the adult viewer right to the very end, called “interpret it however you like”. This isn’t your clear-cut depression or afterlife; good luck working it out here: what does it even mean to be a sea monster?

- I’ve laid on the honey; time to remember to mention the downside too. The ending, to my taste, is mostly made to serve pedagogical considerations (and so it is dull and blurry). You can argue here about what the freedom the heroes strove for so hard really is, and what their friendship meant to each of them. But in terms of meaning the film rather loses out from this “have it both ways” kind of solution. Good thing the film’s merits outweigh it with room to spare.

---

## The History of Concrete: John Wilson Turns His Gaze to the Ground Beneath His Feet

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/istoriya-betona-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-04 (4 June 2026)
Work: “The History of Concrete” is a 2026 film directed by John Wilson.
Tags: documentary, festivals
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/istoriya-betona-2026/

The [Beat Film Festival](https://beatfilmfestival.ru/schedule) (the Moscow documentary festival) kicks off today, and its programme this year is fascinating (some of it is [on Kinopoisk](https://t.me/beatfest/5408) too, Russia’s largest film database and streaming service, so you can watch right at home).

I got an early look at [*The History of Concrete*](https://beatfilmfestival.ru/movies/istoriya-betona) by John Wilson, the creator of the absurdist HBO show *How To with John Wilson*. The director goes on observing the contradictory everyday life of New York, this time turning his gaze to the ground right beneath his feet: to concrete, whose history we as humankind take too little interest in.

He makes this choice in the thick of a creative crisis, after his collaboration with a major streamer has come to an end (the unseen side of creative work gets on camera here too, which we always appreciate). Together with John we find ourselves at a screenwriting masterclass and learn the secrets of making “soap” that’s a hit with mass audiences (*oh God, it made me queasy how the ingredients matched up with* [Heated Rivalry](https://t.me/kino_voice/1213) *point for point, but I pretended not to see or hear a thing*). The director decides to follow the soap-makers’ advice and shoot his own story about concrete on exactly those principles.

His documentary observations take in both scenes from the idiosyncratic corporate life of the concrete industry and rambling conversations with strangers that are at times startling to hear (a couple of them told the director that “there isn’t too much concrete in cities; the problem is that there are now too many people in cities”). Towards the end, the film turns into nothing less than a philosophical reflection on the fragility of human nature in our material-to-the-core world. In short, you definitely won’t come away without a discovery or two — don’t miss it if you like looking at the world from a new angle. And I’ll be back with other gems from the programme.

---

## The Story of His Maid: A Modern-Minded Costume Drama with a Sense of Humour

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/istoriya-ego-sluzhanki-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-02 (2 June 2026)
Work: “The Story of His Maid” is a 2026 series directed by Vlad Nikolaev, Anna Lobanova, Nikolay Burlak.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, melodrama, costumes
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/istoriya-ego-sluzhanki-serial/

The first episode of [*The Story of His Maid*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1410) (*Istoriya ego sluzhanki*) sets out the show’s strengths straight away.

This is genre storytelling through and through, with every ingredient of a costume drama done the modern way, so fans of the genre will enjoy it. The 19th-century interiors and costumes are wonderful, yet the characters’ speech is modernised here and there and present-day music is dropped in. The pace is tuned to a modern audience too: you might expect a story about the nobility and their affairs of the heart to be slow going, but not this one. The 50 minutes of the first episode flew by.

And above all there is humour — even more of it than I expected. My favourite character so far is Potap, Count Sheremetyev’s servant, who will play Captain Obvious one minute and ~~defuse~~ make an awkward situation even more awkward the next. In general, the supporting characters are lively and likeable; the world gains depth, and with it you start to trust what is happening.

## Which Moped with Chrome-plated Handlebars…: Word-Juggling That Is Off the Charts

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/malenkiy-moped-s-khromirovannym-rulem-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-06-01 (1 June 2026)
Work: “Which Moped with Chrome-plated Handlebars at the Back of the Yard?” is a 1966 book by Georges Perec.
Tags: books
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/malenkiy-moped-s-khromirovannym-rulem-kniga/

A book break

I seized the chance to bring a long-forgotten pleasure back into my life: reading a book (a paper one!!) on the beach. The text I picked wasn’t a carefree one, mind you, but quite the opposite, one that hides existential horror under a thick layer of post-irony (and who are we to forget about cognitive dissonance on a day off?)

**Which Moped with Chrome-plated Handlebars at the Back of the Yard?** is a novella by Georges Perec that teeters on the line between unbearable lightness and unliftable absurdity. This author’s skill at artful word-juggling is off the charts; I’m now running off to read all his other texts. On that note, by the way, it’s only right to also mention Vladislav Kirichenko, who translated the novella into Russian: this seems to be one of those cases where the text only gained from translation.

The novella’s plot is simple: a gang of Parisian intellectual scenesters who spend days on end holding court in cafés help a pal wriggle out of being called up for the Algerian War. Well, France had one of those in the 1950s and 60s, which is when the story takes place — they were fond of sending conscripts there. And so, in a whirl of endless banter and cynical haggling with the circumstances they find themselves in, the characters live through a moral adventure that ought, by rights, to chill the blood (but the author takes great care to spare us that). The events themselves are, in essence, not all that important, but the way they are written about is the main thing, the very reason the book is worth reading.

---

## Posle Fishera. Inkvizitor: A Tightly Packed Start with Familiar (Bar One) Character Types

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/posle-fishera-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-28 (28 May 2026); updated: 2026-06-29
Work: “Posle Fishera. Inkvizitor” is a 2026 series directed by Olga Frenkel.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, mystery
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/posle-fishera-serial/

## 28 May 2026

[*Posle Fishera*](https://youtu.be/XAhopBYx78w?si=fEpcyXL-k_2bBB_P) («После Фишера», “After Fisher”, the continuation of the hit crime series *Fisher*) gets off to a very tightly packed start, with familiar (bar one) character types.

In place of Bokov, the resident bad cop is investigator Belova, played by Yulia Snigir. There is also an excessively cheerful second investigator, Terekhov (Alexander Petrov), who at first is very reminiscent of Yatsenko’s character in the first seasons. The forest girl played by Polina Gukhman, on the other hand, is something entirely new in this universe. This literally wild character is perhaps the main source of interest in the season ahead right now. And the casting is just perfect, a real find.

The premise — a murder that leads to the investigation of a whole chain of similar crimes — is clear enough; that, too, is a pretty classic ingredient here. Its distinctive character comes largely from the forest landscapes and the infighting among the detectives themselves, which is already intriguing and makes you want to keep watching. I’m making a wish for the same kind of screenwriting finds [in the way the characters speak](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/fisher-zatmenie-serial/) that made the second season such a joy :)

By the way, props for the cover of Mumiy Troll’s song “Eto po lyubvi” (“It’s for Love”) in the opening credits: I’m not usually thrilled by reworkings, but this one is spot on.

## 8 June 2026

And [*Posle Fishera*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1501) has really got up to speed in its second episode.

What I especially like is how all the offshoots of the plot are coming together into one big, intricately woven chain: there were some fears that the whole thing might fall apart, but now they won’t come true :) And, by the way, although the series is just a little short on the 1990s-and-2000s “charm” we know from the previous seasons, the root of all the trouble still lies in exactly that era: the flashbacks to 2006 are now into their second episode, and 1993 comes up in conversation too. The gold standard, in short, is being upheld.

And some chemistry, of a sort, has started to appear between the two sleuths. In the first episode you couldn’t feel enough mutual hatred to motivate them to solve cases. But now it’s there, and I hope it carries on in the same vein.

## 29 June 2026

With three episodes to go before the end of the season, [*Posle Fishera*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1541) leaves viewers a certain amount of room for thought.

The detective plot has firmed up (as has the working relationship between Snigir’s and Petrov’s characters), and Tonka, played by Polina Gukhman, has made her presence felt too. And — most unexpected of all — Belova’s daughter (Taisya Kalinina), who earlier seemed no more than a passing detail of the investigator’s life story, has taken a fully fledged place among the supporting characters. Now her influence on the situation has a noticeable effect on the storylines of almost all the characters.

I’m even nagged by the thought: might the next plot twist be the moment when Belova has to choose between her own daughter and her newly acquired one (in the shape of Tonka)? The script clearly still has room to manoeuvre, so I wouldn’t rule out that turn of events either.

## I Love You Phillip Morris: From Wily High Jinks to Penitent Misery

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ya-lyublyu-tebya-filipp-morris-2009/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-25 (25 May 2026)
Work: “I Love You Phillip Morris” is a 2009 film directed by Glenn Ficarra, John Requa.
Tags: comedy, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ya-lyublyu-tebya-filipp-morris-2009/

*I watched a film that only its makers and I remember*.

It’s the dramedy **I Love You Phillip Morris** with Jim Carrey and Ewan McGregor. When you first see this film, you think: why did they never show it on STS (the Russian TV channel)? It’s got Jim Carrey in it, hasn’t it?

But half an hour in, you understand everything (though that aspect, naturally, is not the main thing at all).

The film is built in an unusual way: from the very start the hero faces no colossal task or danger. We simply watch him trying to fit into a world where even just living quietly in your own way takes effort, never mind reaching any great heights (though he strives for those too).

Vibe-wise it is somewhat like **Better Call Saul** and **Liar Liar**, which also stars Carrey. In other words, what we have is a supremely charming trickster who still pays for every deft manoeuvre with bitter tears. And so we lurch along with the hero from wily high jinks to penitent misery — which always works like the most thrilling of fairground rides.

Notably, the film has no firm ending: the hero seems destined to go on wriggling like this for the rest of his life. So there is, in my view, certainly more drama than comedy in this dramedy (which is always convincing).

---

## Apex: Working Through Grief, or a Thrill Ride with Two Maniacs

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/na-vershine-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-23 (23 May 2026)
Work: “Apex” is a 2026 film directed by Baltasar Kormákur.
Tags: thriller, American cinema, streaming
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/na-vershine-2026/

True victim of social media that I am, I gave [*Apex*](https://youtu.be/kgv8jf_8dm0?is=OwSeXDsriI3GteRo) a watch (in Russian, «На вершине», “At the Top”).

The Chemical Brothers song that went viral thanks to the film had started turning up in my feed far too often (spoiler: that was indeed the best scene in the film).

Well, I may have thought everyone was done watching adrenaline junkies back at Tom Cruise’s filmography, but Netflix thinks otherwise. The heroine, Sasha (Charlize Theron), loses her husband on an extreme mountain climb and, six months later, still working through the loss, decides to conquer a raging river — on her own this time. Yes, her loss has done nothing whatsoever to change her relationship with extreme sports.

Along the way Sasha meets Ben (Taron Egerton) — a sweet young man at first, who naturally turns out to be a maniac and puts Sasha through a “survivality” show in the rainforest. The most interesting thing about the plot is how their relationship transforms over the course of their shared adventure.

Shot as a thriller, the story can be watched either as the heroine working through her grief or as a thrill ride in which two maniacs from opposite ends of the spectrum have found each other. Either way, your curiosity never flags, because there’s no predicting how on earth it will all end.

## Off Campus: Echoes of Heated Rivalry and a Suspicious “Nothing Serious”

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vne-kampusa-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-22 (22 May 2026)
Work: “Off Campus” is a 2026 series directed by Silver Tree, Sam Bailey, Erica Dunton, Dawn Wilkinson.

Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vne-kampusa-serial/

Having read [Olya’s recommendation](https://t.me/kinokotik/13570), I took the plunge and started watching [*Off Campus*](https://youtu.be/4Vin2GSA4V0?si=4pa593qGF3gNcZaN) — a romantic series about a straight-A student who strikes a deal (to fake a relationship) with a hotshot hockey player (oh-ho, look alive, everyone) in order to get the attention of her real crush. ~~(Naturally, we conclude at once that the heroine’s taste leaves something to be desired, since her crush isn’t a hockey player)~~

2 episodes watched. At first I was just spotting interesting overlaps with [*Heated Rivalry*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1213) for a laugh:

- An awkward scene in the gym showers
- A gold chain that never comes off (no cross on it, I looked closely, but I’ll count it anyway)
- Daddy issues
- A sad story involving the mother
- A made-up name for a contact in the phone
- “Nothing serious, it’s simple”

And it was at that last item (by the middle of the second episode) that I tensed up. We know all about your “nothing serious” and your fun and games. After a carefree start like this you usually find yourself sobbing by around episode 6. Especially given the constant flashbacks the two leads keep having. We’ll see what comes of it.

## The Drama: An Object Lesson in Broken Tolerance

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/vot-eto-drama-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-16 (16 May 2026)
Work: “The Drama” is a 2026 film directed by Kristoffer Borgli.
Tags: drama, rom-com
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/vot-eto-drama-2026/

For me, [*The Drama*](https://youtu.be/6zmKcUa4Xxk?si=1GDxOxemZpXz_RDH) proved a stunningly illustrative film about broken tolerance. And absolute cinema when it comes to artistic exaggeration, too.

This anti-rom-com with Zendaya and Robert Pattinson has a lot of things with the prefix “over”. An over-reaction to the heroine’s confession of the worst thing she has ever done (paradoxically, it isn’t even something she did, only thoughts). An over-concentration of infuriating traits in the newlyweds’ best friend, played by Alana Haim: her character is expressly engineered for the audience to hate, and I don’t even know how I’ll watch *Licorice Pizza* now, with the same actress in the lead. The over-susceptibility of Pattinson’s character to the opinions of those around him: I’m sure that if he and his fiancée had had this conversation in private, and not to the drunken whooping of friends who had themselves started this exchange of confessions, it would all have gone far more peacefully.

And what looks most warped of all is the context it all happens in. In a world where everyone is capable of forgiving acts ranging from cyberbullying to everyday sadism on merely hearing how old the culprit was at the time (like, 15 — no brains yet), it proves impossible to accept the existence of thoughts about something worse than their own nasty deeds. The director, Kristoffer Borgli, shows how hard it turns out to be, in an age of universal tolerance, to show tolerance towards precisely this: dissent from the social norm (even if it was never backed up by actions). Worse still is watching the groom, who under pressure from society is ready to give up “the love of his life” at a stroke. No comment.

Conclusions? The film is an excellent social horror. The main characters could have used the proverb “let bygones be bygones” (the Russian version runs: whoever brings up the past loses an eye).

---

## The Hustler: Everything Is Terrific, but the Ending Is a Slight Letdown

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kommersant-2026/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-15 (15 May 2026); updated: 2026-06-11
Work: “The Hustler” is a 2026 film directed by Fedor Kravchuk, Nikita Kravchuk.
Tags: Russian cinema, drama, crime
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kommersant-2026/

## 15 May 2026

Everything about the film [*The Hustler*](https://youtu.be/Bltzllpag7Y?si=s517AoiBZWCOh4tz) (*Kommersant*) is terrific, but the ending is a slight letdown (for me)

There’s plenty that’s great in this story of a big-shot banker who, through a combination of none-too-pleasant circumstances, ends up in prison.

**1️⃣** First, every 15 minutes (literally) a fresh disaster comes crashing down on Alexander Petrov’s character: arrest, prison, betrayal, and it only gets worse from there. It comes across as not just gripping but realistic: life does have situations you can’t shake off for years, because they only grow with every attempt to resolve them.

**2️⃣** Second, the acting, the production design and the visuals serve the script just perfectly: convincing enough, and yet cinematic enough not to turn the whole thing into a mockumentary.

**3️⃣** Third, I want to single out, as a point of its own, the character played by Husky (the rapper): Slava the *smotryashchiy* (the inmate who runs the cell block). The last time I saw anyone nail the gangster type so distinctively, right down to the intonation, was Ruzil Minekaev in *The Boy’s Word*.

As for the ending. I won’t spoil it, but the idea that the hero supposedly chose the right path in life and never sank beneath human dignity strikes me as inconsistent. In the second half of the film he gives an enemy from his prison cell a literal kicking, because the situation and the basic notion of self-defence demanded it. Wasn’t that a spiritual fall, and revenge pure and simple? So the protagonist is capable of showing his enemies “reciprocity” too, then? Whereas with the business partner who cheated him out of his money and several lost years of his life, mercy, it seems, kicked in. All in all, the denouement is beautiful, but it certainly doesn’t match the realism of the rest of the film.

P.S.: One thought won’t leave me alone. At the end the protagonist says he never saw his former friend again, and at the decisive moment of their showdown on the outside Slava the smotryashchiy seemed to meet him halfway in the absurd impulse not to kill. It is quite likely that off screen the “friend’s” fate was settled after all, just not in front of Andrey.

## 20 May 2026

I’ve [set out](https://www.kinopoisk.ru/media/article/4012757/) here why [*The Hustler*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1481) turned out so great.

It turns out it all comes down to a coincidence of debuts and the blessing of the author of the book it is based on. Only joking, of course: it’s all far more complicated.

What actually went into it was:

- the legacy of Anna Mons (the mistress of Peter the Great)
- associations with a packed metro carriage
- learning *fenya* (Russian criminal slang) to native-speaker level

This is definitely a film with a rich history behind it.

## 11 June 2026

And if you need a plan for what to watch tonight, take a look at the digital release of the film [*The Hustler*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1481).

The crime drama with Alexander Petrov and Husky is a pleasure to watch thanks to its pace and its distinctive editing ([I wrote about this here](https://t.me/kino_voice/1491)). But it will be even more of a pleasure to hit pause and pore over the details: believe me, the film is rich in them. And the characters aren’t the obvious kind, so they are interesting to watch. It’s no accident that *The Hustler* set every record, possible and impossible, at the box office.

---

## Lawyers: Lively, Punchy Dialogue — a Laugh and a Lesson in One

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/advokaty-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-12 (12 May 2026); updated: 2026-05-29
Work: “Lawyers” is a 2026 series directed by Anna Parmas, Leonid Telezhinskiy.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, dramedy, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/advokaty-serial/

## 12 May 2026

[*Lawyers*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/prezentatsiya-kion-advokaty-bar/) (*Advokaty*) now has a teaser trailer

The dramedy from Kion (a Russian streaming service) about champions of the common people, with Ekaterina Vilkova (Lyudmila, a seasoned lawyer) and Eldar Kalimulin (Artyom, an ambitious assistant), won my heart back at the platform’s presentation, and its premiere is getting close :) Vibe-wise, I’m hoping for a spiritual heir to **_Better Call Saul_ and _Nevernye_** («Неверные», “The Unfaithful”), if both of those series were comedies.

Also turning up on screen (partly, I suspect, in the guise of eccentric clients) will be Aglaya Tarasova, Ruslan Bratov, Miloš Biković and Anna Mikhalkova. All in all, it sounds promising.

And here is what Eldar Kalimulin says about his character:

*The most important thing about my character is his sincerity, his faith in people and his wish to follow the letter of the law up to a certain point. To my mind, lawyers are a kind of legal rock star. There’s a similarity between acting and advocacy, too. We work a lot with an audience, with text, with all sorts of sources… There’s a desire in us to get to the truth.*

## 29 May 2026

I really enjoyed the first two episodes of [*Lawyers*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1478), a series about the absurd daily grind of the consultants at a law firm.

For all that it simplifies the profession here and there, *Lawyers* has lively, punchy dialogue (Vilkova’s character, for one, masterfully cuts her ex-husband down to size with every line), and on the educational side there are passages from Russian law, quoted liberally in pop-up boxes on screen. So you get a laugh and a lesson, it seems, and these days forewarned is forearmed.

As for the cast, everyone is in exactly the right place: playing a hapless boss suits Ruslan Bratov, and Anna Kotova is just right as that colleague so many of us know, the one who can’t live without her passive-aggressive pet names :) I’ll keep watching and emptying my head (so as to fill it up with fresh legal norms)

## The Devil Wears Prada: Andy Loses a Point for Lacking a Journalist’s Curiosity

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/dyavol-nosit-prada-2006/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-10 (10 May 2026)
Work: “The Devil Wears Prada” is a 2006 film directed by David Frankel.
Tags: rewatch, comedy
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/dyavol-nosit-prada-2006/

I spent yesterday evening rewatching **The Devil Wears Prada**, so today I ~~am studying the brand’s website~~ have a few observations to share. There will definitely be spoilers below, so if by any chance you want to avoid them while reading about a 20-year-old film, tread carefully.

- Andy (Anne Hathaway) turning up to apply for a job at a fashion glossy having prepared nothing but her brilliant CV, with its line about being editor-in-chief of the university newspaper, is either a mark of a bygone approach to hiring or glaring irresponsibility on the heroine’s part. If it’s the former, then we have, it turns out, lost the chance to get by on professional skills alone, without also having to elbow each other aside over expertise in a particular outlet’s subject. If it’s the latter, then Andy simply went about things unprofessionally. Just as any self-respecting journalist prepares for an interview with a particular subject, shaping the conversation around that very person, so when you go for a job at a fashion glossy the natural thing would be to do your homework, enough to know the name Gabbana. Here Andy loses a point from me for lacking the most basic journalistic curiosity.

- Andy’s love life also made me want to go over it from the standpoint of logic. If the attraction between her and the big-name journalist has already become mutual, why run away from him, slamming the door (and, let’s admit it, giving up a certain set of career perks)? If she wants to get back together with her original boyfriend, shedding the job with no fixed hours in the process, why take a job in New York instead of going to Boston with him? The film handles the romance far more schematically than the career: the heroine’s men turn quite literally into symbols, either of career temptation and intrigue (Christian the journalist) or of simplicity and naivety outside the glossy world (Nate the boyfriend). With that much schematising, I dread to think what will become of the heroine’s love life in the second film.

- Surprisingly enough, the characters I’ll find most interesting in the sequel are Emily and Nigel. They are full of contradictions, both are, to a certain degree, charismatic in a villainous way and, when it comes down to it, deeper than either Andy or Miranda. In essence, they are the ones who personify the world of glossy magazines in the film, embodying its pros and cons.

- No questions for Miranda Priestly. That’s all.

---

## Ssora: The Paradoxes of Love After 20 Years Together

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ssora-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-08 (8 May 2026)
Work: “Ssora” is a series directed by Klim Kozinsky.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, announcements, drama
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/ssora-serial/

I’m poring over the first stills from the set of *Ssora* («Ссора», “The Quarrel”) from Kion (a Russian streaming service).

Klim Kozinsky’s new series (my impressions of his [*First Issue*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pervyy-nomer-serial/) are still fresh) will be about the paradoxes of love. > I’ve seen a lot of different family relationships in my life, but I’ve never come across one like the one we are playing. And yet our on-screen family relationship somehow looks recognisable, possible, perfectly real. But in life I don’t do a single one of the things that the man I play does.

## Kniga Utkina: A Text as Many-Sided as Its Subject

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/kniga-utkina-my-tut-zhizn-zhivem-kniga/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-05-07 (7 May 2026)
Work: “Kniga Utkina: My tut zhizn zhivyom” is a 2026 book by Vasily Utkin, Stanislav Gridasov.
Tags: books, sport
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/kniga-utkina-my-tut-zhizn-zhivem-kniga/

Hello to everyone whose night went better than mine (I’ve been unable to fly out of Vnukovo airport since midnight, but that’s a whole other story).

What’s getting me through is the half-autobiography, half-biopic of Vasily Utkin (the legendary Russian sports commentator) called [*Kniga Utkina: My tut zhizn zhivyom*](https://books.yandex.ru/books/hAVI33lR) («Книга Уткина: Мы тут жизнь живем», “The Utkin Book: We Live Life Here”). It’s a read that is a complete patchwork in structure and style, combining yarns from the great man’s life, first-hand testimony to how sports journalism took shape in the 1990s, and utterly charming details of Utkin’s biography as seen by those who worked alongside him. In short, the text has turned out as many-sided as its subject, and a huge inspiration to go and do great things.

One detail took the shine off my delight, and that is the way the audio version of *Kniga Utkina* is packaged. I’m highly sceptical of audiobooks and almost never listen to them, because there’s always something that isn’t to my liking. This time I decided (inspired, apparently, by Vasily’s openness) to have a listen, and was instantly let down. Each chapter opens with a peculiar jingle that pairs perky music in the style of the *Uralskie Pelmeni* opening theme (the Russian TV comedy show) with stock sounds of shouting fans. And that is completely (with all due respect to both ingredients) out of keeping with the spirit of the book. The book presents Utkin as a subtle, passionate and witty man who, sadly, left us very early. So hearing that sort of “playful” compèring before, say, a philosophical chapter by Yuri Saprykin doesn’t just wreck whatever mood you were in — it is simply out of place :(

So I highly recommend the book — only not to listen to, but to actually read.

---

## First Racket: A Nearly Burnt-Out Coach and Gripping Match Scenes

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/pervaya-raketka-serial/

Work: “First Racket” is a 2026 series directed by Evgeny Korchagin.

[*First Racket*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1379) («Первая ракетка») wastes no time on exposition and drops you straight into its characters’ story: a nearly burnt-out tennis coach (Kozlovsky) and a player who has gone off the rails (Gukhman).

The reasons for the coach’s inner turmoil are not entirely clear yet, but his arc is already interesting to watch. Danila Kozlovsky (whose birthday is today, by the way) is, as ever, great at flipping from disillusionment to a fire in his eyes. Polina Gukhman’s heroine keeps secrets from everyone; as they come out, the character is sure to show new sides.

And the momentum comes from the match scenes, which are convincing and gripping here.

## Half Man: The Finale Is Worth Watching for One Scene and One Character

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/half-man-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova
Published: 2026-04-30 (30 April 2026); updated: 2026-05-31
Work: “Half Man” is a 2026 series directed by Alexandra Brodski, Eshref Reybrouck.
Tags: series, drama, thriller
Translated from Russian with AI assistance; original: https://kinovoice.com/reviews/half-man-serial/

## 30 April 2026

*\*she spent two days working out how to write about this series\**

[*Half Man*](https://youtu.be/egkRy1U94tA?si=i7wxU7hOzcE0Fsfr) takes a full swing at your nerves with a heap of hints that have no single reading — with uncertainty, in other words, which is harder to bear than some tortures. A series about the difficult relationship between two men who are, in effect, stepbrothers plays far more strikingly than it sounds in summary, precisely because both leads are so ambiguous. How each of them sees the other is quite the puzzle.

Richard Gadd, the writer and producer of this story, who previously impressed everyone with [*Baby Reindeer*,](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ya-znayu-kto-tebya-ubil-serial/) has undergone a colossal change of image. He is no longer the “doormat” type but, on the contrary, Ruben, a hard man who radiates an aura of danger for a kilometre around. For everyone, that is, except Niall, the brother that circumstance has handed him, a man of far more modest physical and moral build. He, incidentally, is the one the deer nickname has stuck to (something Richard, it seems, has no intention of giving up in his shows). The story of their relationship runs from adolescence towards one specific moment in adult life, which comes across as the most chilling stretch of the first episode.

You could call *Half Man* a coming-of-age story, a drama about toxic masculinity, even a psychological thriller. What matters most is the speed with which the series seizes your attention, leaving you no chance of passing on the second episode.

## 6 May 2026

The second episode of [*Half Man*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1447) leaves the distinct impression that this could have been a very funny comedy of errors, if the consequences of everything the characters do were not so utterly realistic. In essence, it is that very step from comedy to tragedy, and *Half Man* takes it in the direction of the latter.

As in the previous episode, most of the screen time goes to the young versions of the leads, Mitchell Robertson (Niall) and Stuart Campbell (Ruben), and they do, of course, turn in tremendously strong work. They are joined by the young incarnation of another important character, Albie, played by Bilal Hasna. I think we’ll 100% be seeing some of these names in the coming awards season.

As for the famous discomfort of watching it, which the series has already made its name on, it comes in patches, sometimes giving way to moments that are, if anything, too bright. Which makes it all the more painful to ride this rollercoaster back down into the hell of the uncontrollable catastrophe that engulfs the characters time after time. And, it has to be said, 70% of the anxiety comes down simply to the presence (not the words, not even the actions) of Richard Gadd, the adult version of Ruben: he turns your stomach worse than any cruelty shown on screen.

## 11 May 2026

The midpoint of the [*Half Man*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1464) season is marked by a tremendously powerful episode (possibly the most powerful of the whole season). And by a no less impressive cliffhanger at the end of it. In short, the psychological thriller we deserve.

As was bound to happen, a conflict that at first seemed entirely black and white has drifted into shades of grey. Of all the parties, it seems, only Albie comes across as wholly unambiguous — and even then, as the series has taught us by now, with the caveat “for now”.

And now we also have an idea of how the making of a single decision can be turned into one big 50-minute doubt, complicated by a sense of guilt that keeps welling up. It sits very neatly within the high concept of a series about how the years gone by shape one particular day in the future.

## 19 May 2026

Something interesting is going on with Richard Gadd’s series.

In [*Baby Reindeer*](https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/ya-znayu-kto-tebya-ubil-serial/) an important part of the plot turned on how the life of a victim of traumatic events goes on to build itself around the original catastrophe, and at what price healing comes (and even then, not always).

In [*Half Man*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1476), by contrast, judging by the fourth episode, we are starting to get hints: aren’t we fixating on our trauma a bit too much? Maybe it’s time to stop replaying how somebody hurt and insulted us, and get on with our own lives instead? Because years on, the difference between the one who found the strength to move on and the one who chose to stay in the victim’s costume is colossal. Both men, who for many years saw themselves as victims, end up living radically different lives, and you can’t watch that unmoved. It feels especially relevant when we are faced with global crises that traumatise everyone.

Quite a curious circle the moral of the story has turned between 2024 and 2026, I must say.

## 31 May 2026

The final episode of [*Half Man*](https://t.me/kino_voice/1489) is worth watching for one scene and one character (who isn’t even in it).

The couple of things revealed about the past did not, by and large, play any part in moving the plot along. We already knew who Niall was marrying, and had already seen that Ruben was at the wedding without his family. The fatal outcome of the fight in the shed was shown back in episode 5, so that was hardly going to surprise anyone either.

One particular moment closed the loop on this whole string of absurd self-harm, done to their own lives and other people’s. Ruben and Niall’s last conversation in prison, through a wall of clear plastic, is the nervous breakdown of both men, expressed with stunning economy. Their whole fate over a couple of decades boils down to a brief list of facts that are hard to say, or to hear, without laughing at the absurdity of it. The whole thing is like some sad joke.

And then I [remembered](https://t.me/kino_voice/1505) just what “joke” would fit here. There is nothing worse than building your life around an attempt to guess what the person next to you is thinking (even if that urge does come from past trauma). There is nothing funnier or more pointless than years and decades spent in that mode. One character did manage to break out of the vicious circle: Albie. His life and his health were wrecked; physically and morally, he was literally trampled. And here is this man 20 years on, as if nothing had happened, smiling, meeting people halfway, ready to give them chances. I’m sure that off screen he has lived full years, thanks to being honest with himself and demanding that honesty from those around him (rather than trying to “work it out for himself”). For me, I think, he is the one who will remain the main character of this story.

---

## Radar: Soviet Schoolchildren Alone with the Supernatural

URL: https://kinovoice.com/en/reviews/radar-serial/
Author: Betsy Isakova

Work: “Radar” is a 2026 series directed by Konstantin Smirnov.
Tags: series, Russian cinema, science fiction, music
